metadata.title: cordova-plugin-file-transfer Alternative for Capacitor
metadata.description: Replace cordova-plugin-file-transfer in Capacitor apps: @capacitor/file-transfer for simple transfers, Capgo uploader and downloader for background jobs.
metadata.author: Martin Donadieu
metadata.head_image_alt: Illustration of migrating a Cordova app to Capacitor, used for a file transfer plugin guide
metadata.keywords: cordova-plugin-file-transfer alternative, capacitor file transfer, capacitor upload file, capacitor download file, background upload capacitor, @capacitor/file-transfer, @capgo/capacitor-uploader

faq.question: Is cordova-plugin-file-transfer deprecated?
faq.answer: Apache announced in 2017 that it planned to deprecate it in favor of XMLHttpRequest Level 2, but the plugin is not marked deprecated on npm and received releases in 2023 (2.0.0) and August 2026 (2.0.1). In Capacitor apps it still depends on cordova-plugin-file and file:// paths, so native Capacitor plugins are the better fit.

faq.question: What should I use instead of cordova-plugin-file-transfer in Capacitor?
faq.answer: Use @capacitor/file-transfer for foreground uploads and downloads with progress. Use @capgo/capacitor-uploader and @capgo/capacitor-downloader when transfers must continue in the background, be retried, paused or resumed.

faq.question: Why not just use fetch or XMLHttpRequest?
faq.answer: Web requests load the whole file into WebView memory as a Blob or ArrayBuffer and pass it across the bridge. Large videos or archives can crash the WebView, and requests stop when the app is suspended. Native transfers stream from and to disk.

faq.question: Can I cancel or pause a transfer?
faq.answer: @capacitor/file-transfer has no cancel method. @capgo/capacitor-uploader can cancel with removeUpload, and @capgo/capacitor-downloader supports pause, resume and stop.

faq.question: Do transfers continue if the user closes the app?
faq.answer: Capgo's uploader uses a background URLSession on iOS and a foreground upload service with a notification on Android, and the downloader uses the platform background download APIs, so transfers can continue after the app is backgrounded. @capacitor/file-transfer runs while the app is active.
